gloss: offering (to gods, Buddha, or the deceased)

definitions.gloss: offering (to gods, Buddha, or the deceased)
definitions.explanation: Food, drink, or other items placed before a shrine, altar, or grave as a religious or spiritual offering.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{供|そな}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}いた→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: I placed an offering on the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{供|そな}え{餅|もち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}ります→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: We display kagami mochi as an offering at New Year.

examples.japanese: お{供|そな}え⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げて→下げる：00807_sageru⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: We took down the fruit offering and the family ate it together.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{命日|めいにち}→命日：17539_meinichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{供|そな}え⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だった⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}んだ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
examples.english: I chose Japanese sweets that my grandfather liked as an offering on his memorial day.

notes:
Refers to items offered to deities, Buddhist figures, or ancestors. The word uses the honorific prefix お and the noun form of ⟦{供|そな}える→供える：11562_sonaeru⟧ (to offer). After being offered, items are often "taken down" (⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧) and consumed by the family, which is considered respectful sharing of divine blessings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{供|そな}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧: make an offering
- お{供|そな}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧: take down an offering (to eat it)
- お{供|そな}え{餅|もち}: offering rice cakes (kagami mochi)
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}: offering items (formal)
- ⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{供|そな}え: altar offerings

CULTURAL NOTE:
Common offerings include rice, fruit, sweets, sake, and water. At New Year, stacked round mochi called ⟦{鏡餅|かがみもち}→鏡餅：19469_kagamimochi⟧ are placed as offerings. The act of eating offerings after they have been presented is called お⟦{下|さ}がり→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧, and is seen as receiving blessings from the deity or ancestor.
